# Cleanup logger

## Pull Request by @tomusdrw

Closes #805 

I've noticed an issue with filtering specific log entries, which was caused by a bug introduced by padding module names.

This PR fixes this bug and introduces some tests. To make writing tests easier I also implemented #805.

## Walkthrough

This pull request restructures the logger module from a monolithic implementation to a modular, re-export-based architecture. A new Logger class is introduced in `logger.ts` with global configuration management, per-module log level resolution, and six logging methods (insane, trace, log, info, warn, error). The public API in `index.ts` is reorganized to re-export from four separate modules (console.js, logger.js, options.js, transport.js) instead of directly exporting a local Logger class. A TransportBuilder type is added to `transport.ts` for custom transport implementations. Test coverage is introduced with a new test suite validating logger functionality including level dispatch, configuration, and module-based filtering.

## Estimated code review effort

🎯 3 (Moderate) | ⏱️ ~20 minutes

- **Logger class design**: Verify static configuration methods, per-module level resolution logic, and level caching mechanism for correctness
- **Re-export strategy in index.ts**: Ensure the modular re-export approach maintains backward compatibility and doesn't create circular dependencies
- **Transport integration**: Confirm TransportBuilder type signature and integration with ConsoleTransport works as intended
- **Test coverage gaps**: Review whether the MockTransport implementation and test cases provide sufficient coverage of edge cases (e.g., multi-module logging, dynamic reconfiguration)

- **FluffyLabs/typeberry#656**: Modifies logger API at code level—changes Logger method signatures to tagged-template form and updates Transport/ConsoleTransport interfaces accordingly
